summary: Adds private customer documentation workspaces with verified-domain or individual-reader admission, checked on every protected request.
userImpact: Publishers can admit verified accounts at exact approved email domains automatically, or require additional expiring individual grants.

instructions: Roll out the account contract before enabling customer documentation bundles.

configuration: Adds optional private EG_DOCUMENTATION_WORKSPACES_JSON. accessMode verified_domain admits current verified exact-domain accounts without individual grants; the default explicit_readers mode retains individual expiry checks. Both default to no configured workspaces. Policy changes require rollout to every runtime instance.

changes: Adds customer workspace discovery, scoped session authorization and workspaceContract capability metadata for deployment preflight.

notes: Reuses existing verified accounts and exact session rows; no tenants or grants are inferred from application memberships.

security: General documentation access never authorizes customer content.

Every asset rechecks the current verified email, account, source session and exact configured workspace domain. Domain admission must be explicitly selected; legacy policies retain individual-reader restrictions.
Automatic verified-domain admission requires a centrally verified Cloud account session; another tenant's provider email assertion cannot grant customer access.
knownLimitations: The admission policy is publisher-managed deployment configuration. There is no grant administration UI or automatic upstream AD group provisioning.
Existing upstream account revocation and directory reconciliation determine when upstream AD changes become locally visible.
rollback: Remove customer bundles before rolling back the account contract. An older account response cannot authorize a customer-scoped read.
validation: Local auth routes and domain-authority regression tests cover automatic domain admission, other-domain/subdomain denial, unverified/disabled accounts, policy removal, tenant-provider spoofing and legacy individual-grant compatibility.
Exact gateway/account HTTP qualification with owned PostgreSQL: 2 files and 3 tests passed, including both customers and protected pages, search, downloads, JavaScript and receipts.
Backend host/shared build, backend TypeScript check and affected lint passed. Portal compilation/browser, publication and infrastructure gates are recorded separately in their owning repositories.
No hosted CI, live rollout or customer-content publication is claimed by this local evidence.
